The plantation drive under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” reflects the Ministry’s continued commitment to sustainability and contributes to the Government’s broader vision of promoting a greener and more sustainable future.

articles.title: Ministry of New & Renewable Energy completes Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6; Implementation Phase to Begin from 2nd October, 2026
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE), along with its CPSUs and Autonomous Institutes, has successfully completed the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 , launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG) for institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in Government offices. The Preparatory Phase was carried out from 15th September to 30th September, 2026 .
During this period, the following activities were undertaken:
i. Identification and disposal of pendency under various parameters.
ii. Review, categorisation and weeding out of physical records as per extant guidelines.
iii. Conduct of cleanliness campaigns for maintaining cleanliness in the Ministry and its PSUs and Autonomous Institutes.
iv. Identification and segregation of e-waste as per MoEFCC guidelines for target setting during the Implementation Phase.
The Ministry, its two CPSUs — Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd. (IREDA) and Solar Energy Corporation of India Ltd. (SECI) — and its three Autonomous Institutes — National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) , National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) and Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy (SSS-NIBE) — actively participated in the preparatory phase.
With the successful completion of this phase, the Ministry is now fully geared up for the Implementation Phase of the Campaign, which will commence from 2nd October, 2026 and continue up to 31st October, 2026 . During this period, sustained efforts will be made to achieve all identified targets and further strengthen the culture of cleanliness and efficiency in Government functioning.

The Preparatory Phase was carried out from 15th September to 30th September, 2026 . Identification and disposal of pendency under various parameters.

CCI approves acquisition of certain equity shareholding in Continuum Green Energy Ltd by Chubu Electric Power Company Netherlands B.V.
articles.full_content:
The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of certain equity shareholding in Continuum Green Energy Limited by Chubu Electric Power Company Netherlands B.V.
The Proposed Combination comprises acquisition of certain equity shareholding in Continuum Green Energy Limited ( Target ) by Chubu Electric Power Company Netherlands B.V. ( Acquirer ) by way of both primary subscription and secondary purchase of the equity shares from Continuum Green Energy Holdings Ltd., Singapore.
The Acquirer is a private limited company, incorporated under the laws of Netherlands and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Chubu Electric Power Co., Inc., Japan ( CHUBU ). The Acquirer is engaged in the activities related to investment, management, financing and treasury related functions for the CHUBU Group. CHUBU is a public limited company listed on recognized stock exchanges in Japan and is engaged in the business of generation, distribution and transmission of power generated through renewable sources such as solar, wind, nuclear etc., among other activities.
The Target is a public limited company incorporated under the laws of India. The Target and its various subsidiaries in India are primarily engaged in the business of sale and generation of power through renewable sources such as wind and solar.

articles.full_content:
Calls for Strict, Coordinated and Time-Bound Enforcement of Air Pollution Control Measures
The Sub-Committee on Safeguarding & Enforcement of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) convened its 26th meeting on 29.09.2026 under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM. The meeting comprehensively reviewed the status of preparedness, enforcement and compliance measures being undertaken by the concerned NCR State Governments/ GNCTD and implementing agencies for targeted abatement of air pollution across the National Capital Region (NCR).
During the meeting, detailed deliberations were held on sector-specific measures and implementation of various statutory directions issued by the Commission. The Sub-committee took stock of the preparedness of Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh for implementation of Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026 and the respective action plans for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning during 2026, with the objective of complete elimination of such incidents. The review also covered measures for crop diversification, promotion of Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), utilisation of crop residue and strengthening of awareness and IEC activities among farmers.
The Sub-Committee undertook a comprehensive review of measures for abatement of vehicular pollution, including actions envisaged under Direction No. 88 dated 23.04.2025, as amended on 17.10.2025, relating to restrictions on entry of BS-IV and below transport and commercial goods vehicles into Delhi. The implementation of Direction No. 93 dated 03.06.2025 concerning migration of buses entering Delhi, including buses operating under All India Tourist Permit and other service regimes, towards cleaner modes was also reviewed.
The meeting further examined the preparedness of NCR State Governments/ GNCTD for installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) systems at Fuel/ CNG stations, in accordance with Direction No. 101 dated 15.05.2026, for enforcement of restrictions on fuelling of vehicles without valid Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) in NCR with effect from 01.10.2026. The Sub-Committee also reviewed enforcement of Direction No. 94 dated 03.06.2025, as amended on 23.12.2025, for fast-tracking cleaner mobility in services provided by motor vehicle aggregators, delivery service providers and e-Commerce entities, including compliance verification through surprise checks.
The status of enforcement against older End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, in compliance with the Supreme Court of India’s order dated 17.12.2025 was also deliberated upon, with emphasis on intensifying action for impounding and scrapping of such vehicles. Further, the sub-committee reviewed progress towards complete phasing out of diesel auto-rickshaws from NCR Districts by 31.12.2026 in accordance with Direction No. 70 dated 30.11.2022. Measures for identification and decongestion of traffic congestion hotspots/ intersections in Delhi and NCR town

Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal launches PRAGATI-50 Initiative including Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre at CSIR-CMERI Durgapur
articles.full_content:
Durgapur, September30, 2026
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal launched the PRAGATI-50 initiative to develop 50 model cities for Swachhata in New Delhi on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), alongside key technology-driven urban cleanliness projects including the 'Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre' at CSIR-CMERI Durgapur. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 (SBM-U 2.0), the PRAGATI-50 framework focuses on key performance indicators (KPIs) and digital monitoring across 50 cities in 24 States to establish visible benchmarks for urban sanitation.
Speaking at the launch ceremony, the Union Minister said “These 50 cities across 24 States will emerge as clean role model cities for the rest of the country, by going beyond their routine sanitation work to demonstrate sustained, high-performance parameters of visible cleanliness.
Highlighting the national significance of the facility, Dr. N. C. Murmu, Director, CSIR-CMERI, stated, “The Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre has been established as a national facility for research, product development, testing, validation, certification, and capacity building in sanitation technologies.”
Key Highlights of Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre
ü National Innovation Hub: Established as a national facility in collaboration with CSIR-CMERI for research, product development, testing, validation, certification, and capacity building in sanitation technologies.
ü Bridging Lab-to-Field: Accelerates the deployment of cutting-edge tech solutions, automation, and machine learning tools into active urban municipal operations.
ü Standardization & Capacity Building: Assists Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) with technical guidelines, model designs, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and GeM categorization for waste management infrastructure.
ü Circular Economy Drive: Promotes resource recovery, occupational safety, and sustainable waste processing toward the goal of garbage-free cities under Viksit Bharat 2047 .

Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems
articles.full_content:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme. This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.
The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand. The scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation with in the States/UTs of India.
The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with total project outlay of Rs.1,86,405 crore, comprising Rs.1,36,378 crore for the development of Intra-State Transmission Systems (InSTS) under GEC-III, Rs.50,000 crore for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The Scheme involves a total Central Financial Support of Rs.54,082 crore. The Central Financial Assistance (CFA) will help in offsetting the Intra-State transmission charges and thus keep the power costs down. Thus, the Government support will ultimately benefit the end users – the citizens of India.
All Greenfield projects under the InSTS component will be implemented through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mode, while brownfield upgradation and network strengthening works will be executed under Cost Plus Basis (CPB). The State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agency, and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) will participate under TBCB on a Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM) model.
The scheme will help in achieving the target of 900 GW installed Non-Fossil capacity by 2035. The scheme will also contribute to long term energy security of the country and promote ecologically sustainable growth by reducing carbon footprint. It will generate large direct & indirect employment in the power sector, manufacturing, and construction industries. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing and deployment will additionally generate employment in the domestic energy storage industry. The scheme will also generate long-term skilled employment in operation, maintenance, and grid management across participating States.

This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories. The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand.

Under the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026, Sanitation System in Raipur to Become More Transparent and Result-Oriented
articles.full_content:
Daily Monitoring of Over 5,000 Beats by Dividing the City into Four Clusters Source Segregation of Waste Is the Most Important Provision of the New Rules: Municipal Corporation Commissioner Sambit Mishra
Raipur, September 30, 2026. With the effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, comprehensive changes are being made in Raipur to render the sanitation system more transparent, accountable, and result-oriented. Raipur Municipal Corporation Commissioner Mr. Sambit Mishra shared details of the key provisions of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and the preparations for their execution in Raipur during a press conference organized by the Press Information Bureau, Raipur.
Mr. Mishra stated that under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs selected 50 cities across the country under PRAGATI-50. The objective is to elevate cleanliness in these cities to a level where it is clearly visible to visitors. Raipur and Bilaspur from Chhattisgarh have been included among these selected cities. He said that in line with the vision of the Central and State Governments, efforts are being made to move beyond routine cleaning and develop a system that delivers visibly clear outcomes on the ground to advance Raipur towards becoming a world-class city.
He informed that under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, waste segregation at source has been made more comprehensive. Along with wet and dry waste, emphasis is now placed on keeping sanitary waste and special care waste separate. Sanitary waste includes items such as diapers and sanitary pads, while special care waste includes batteries, bulbs, tube lights, mercury thermometers, and other such items that require safe handling.
The Commissioner said that citizens should develop the habit of handing over waste in segregated categories. A system to collect all four categories of waste separately is also being developed within the Municipal Corporation’s collection setup. He noted that proper waste segregation at source makes the subsequent processing and disposal operations smoother and enables better recovery of useful resources from waste.
Greater Responsibility for Bulk Waste Generators
Mr. Mishra explained that the new rules outline specific responsibilities for bulk waste generating institutions and premises. Establishments generating large quantities of waste—such as large residential complexes, malls, commercial centers, institutions, hostels, and colleges—now have clearer waste management obligations.
He stated that wet waste generated within such premises should ideally be processed on-site wherever feasible. Systems such as composting or biomethanation can be adopted for this purpose. Similarly, for wastewater reuse, small-scale Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) can be installed as needed to recycle water for gardens and other suitable applications.

Delhi Records Lowest September Average AQI in Five Years; Air Quality Improvement Trend Continues in 2026
articles.full_content:
The improving trend in the overall air quality of Delhi-NCR continues, with Delhi recording its lowest monthly average Air Quality Index (AQI) for September during the current year, as compared to the corresponding period of the last five years, from 2022 to 2026.
The monthly average AQI of Delhi for September during the current year has been recorded at 102, as against 105 in 2025, 105 in 2024, 108 in 2023 and 104 in 2022.
The period from January to September 2026 witnessed the highest number of days with daily average AQI less than 200 (‘Moderate’ category) during the last five years. Delhi recorded 194 such days in 2026, as against 187 days in 2025, 188 days in 2024, 193 days in 2023 and 146 days in 2022.
The period from January to September 2026 also witnessed the lowest number of ‘Poor to Severe+’ days during the last five years, with 79 days in 2026, as against 86 days in 2025, 86 days in 2024, 80 days in 2023 and 127 days in 2022.
The period from January to September 2026 (up to 28.09.2026) has witnessed the joint-lowest average PM2.5 concentration in Delhi compared to the corresponding period since 2022. Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 69 µg/m³ in 2026, as against 69 µg/m³ in 2025, 81 µg/m³ in 2024, 73 µg/m³ in 2023 and 80 µg/m³ in 2022.
The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) is working closely with various stakeholders concerned to take effective measures for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution and to improve air quality in Delhi-NCR. These efforts will be further intensified with an endeavour to improve the air quality scenario in Delhi-NCR in the coming days.

The period from January to September 2026 witnessed the highest number of days with daily average AQI less than 200 (‘Moderate’ category) during the last five years.

articles.full_content:
MoU will facilitate structured framework for sharing relevant information from Udyam Registration ecosystem
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been exchanged between Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), to institutionalize a mechanism for sharing relevant data for the development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register (SBR).
The MoU was signed by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Dalip Singh, Additional Director General, MoSPI, in the presence of senior officers from Ministry of MSME and MoSPI.
Objectives of the MoU:-
-The MoU sets the terms and understanding between the Ministry of MSME and MoSPI in relation to the sharing of unit-wise data of the Udyam Registration available with MSME Department through APIs. The two-way API shall provide data for preparation of National Statistical Business Register (NSBR).
-The MoU will facilitate a structured framework for sharing relevant information from the Udyam Registration ecosystem of the Ministry of MSME with MoSPI. The information will contribute to improving the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information used for statistical purposes.
Statistical Business Register (SBR): An Overview
-The Statistical Business Register (SBR) is a central and regularly updated database of registered statistical units engaged in economic activities within a defined geographical territory. It captures businesses, enterprises, establishments & other relevant economic units, key characteristics of economic units and relationships between different units.
- The SBR serves as foundational infrastructure for the economic statistics system to improve the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information by identifying the target population for economic surveys, supporting survey sample selection, enabling the production of business demography statistics, providing a common framework for business demography-related information, and facilitating integration and consistency across different data sources.

Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Prepares for Special Campaign 6 building on Strong Outcomes Achieved under Special Campaign 5.0
articles.full_content:
The Government of India has announced the launch of Special Campaign 6, to be conducted from 2nd–31st October 2026, with the preparatory phase from 15th–30th September 2026. The campaign will focus on institutionalising cleanliness in Government offices, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management, effective space utilisation and enhancing workplace experience.
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) actively participated in Special Campaign 5.0 with a strong emphasis on cleanliness, records management, space optimisation and disposal of pending references across its offices and institutions. During the campaign, more than 1,836 cleanliness drives were conducted. The Ministry disposed of 3 references from Members of Parliament, 7 Parliament Assurances, 307 Public Grievances and 27 Public Grievance Appeals .
As part of the record management initiatives, 1,250 files were reviewed and 466 files were weeded out . In addition, 658 e-files were reviewed, out of which 266 e-files were closed . These efforts resulted in freeing approximately 4,000 square feet of office space through weeding out of files and disposal of scrap. The disposal of scrap also generated revenue of approximately ₹7.58 lakh .
The collective efforts of MSDE and its attached, autonomous, subordinate and field offices contributed towards creating cleaner and more efficient workplaces, improving record management and optimising available office space. The campaign also strengthened awareness regarding the importance of maintaining a clean office environment and responsible disposal of waste.
In preparation for Special Campaign 6, MSDE has initiated preparatory activities and is coordinating with the nodal officers and stakeholders of its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations and field institutions. The nodal officers are being sensitised regarding the key focus areas of the campaign, including cleanliness, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management in accordance with the applicable E-Waste Management Rules, 2022, space management and enhancement of workplace experience.
The Ministry is committed to carrying forward the momentum generated during Special Campaign 5.0 and contributing significantly to the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through sustainable cleanliness practices, effective disposal of pendency, responsible e-waste management, improved record management and creation of cleaner, more efficient and better-utilised workspaces.

NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities”- an initiative under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission (SSM)
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog organised a national workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities” on 28th September 2026, in collaboration with the Golap Borbora State Institute of Panchayat & Rural Development (GBSIPRD), Government of Assam. The workshop focused on strengthening Panchayats as institutions capable of driving inclusive growth, effective public service delivery, and sustainable development at the grassroots, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
The one-day National Workshop was inaugurated by Shri Atul Bora, Minister, Panchayat & Rural Development Department, Government of Assam, as the Chief Guest; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, as the Guest of Honour; Dr. Ravi Kota, Chief Secretary, Government of Assam; and Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development.
The inaugural session highlighted the importance of decentralised governance, spatial planning, capacity development, digitalisation, and convergence for advancing Viksit Gram Panchayats. The deliberations focused on four key areas: decentralised and spatial planning, grassroots capacity development, spatial planning for priority sectors, and integration of spatial planning into the GPDP process.
Participants discussed the constitutional foundation of Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and Part IX of the Constitution. Discussions also focused on clearer activity mapping, adequate financial resources, appropriate staffing, greater decision-making authority, Gram Sabha participation, and institutional accountability. The workshop emphasised the need to move from a sectoral to a spatial and integrated approach to local development. GIS, geospatial data, village master plans, and digital platforms were discussed for identifying local resources, infrastructure gaps, land-use patterns, and development opportunities. Integrating spatial information with GPDP, eGramSwaraj, and Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) was highlighted as a means of strengthening evidence-based and convergence-oriented planning.
Capacity development and institutional strengthening were also central to the deliberations. Participants emphasised equipping elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries with skills in data interpretation, investment prioritisation, resource mobilisation, convergence, and outcome monitoring. Discussions covered devolution, activity mapping, District Planning Committees, digital and hybrid learning, competency development, and last-mile technical handholding. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam (Member, NITI Aayog) called for a shift from sectoral planning to a spatial planning approach, with greater emphasis on human and social capital and the development of local economic clusters.
The workshop identified priorities including clearer functional devolution and activity mapping, improved fiscal resources and own-source revenue mobilisation, stronger capacity and technical support,

SWACHH BHARAT CAMPAIGN OBSERVED IN AGARTALA MILITARY STATION
articles.full_content:
September 29, Agartala: Demonstrating its steadfast commitment towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and operational health readiness, the Indian Army's Spear Corps organized a comprehensive educational and awareness drive for troops stationed in Agartala on 29 September 2026 as part of the nationwide Swachh Bharat Campaign.
The day-long initiative aimed to reinforce the core values of cleanliness, personal hygiene and ecological mindfulness among service personnel, integrating environmental stewardship into daily military routine and garrison management.
The event commenced with a keynote address detailing the vision, spirit and national significance of the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026'. The talk emphasized that cleanliness is an integral component of military discipline, national pride and operational efficiency.
Dedicated interactive sessions were conducted on environmental conservation. Troops were encouraged to remain actively mindful of their daily actions and habits, highlighting how individual choices directly impact the surrounding ecology. Personnel were urged to adopt energy-efficient habits, reduce resource wastage and preserve local ecosystems.
Recognizing that healthy personnel are fundamental to military readiness, a clinical awareness session on Swachhta was also delivered by the Army's Medical Officer focusing on core operational pillars of Personal Hygiene, Sanitation & Cleanliness among soldiers.
Soldiers were also educated on modern waste management protocols centered around the core principles of Reduce, Reuse, Recycle and Recharge. Special emphasis was laid on reducing plastic waste, recycling organic materials and recharging groundwater reserves through rainwater harvesting units within military stations. An Army Official when contacted said, "Cleanliness and environmental responsibility are force multipliers that directly contribute to troop morale, health and operational readiness. Through initiatives under Swachh Bharat Campaign, the Spear Corps remains committed to leading by example in preserving our ecosystems and ensuring the highest standards of sanitation across all garrisons."
Spear Corps of the Indian Army is tasked with maintaining operational readiness and security across the North-Eastern frontier. Beyond its tactical duties, Spear Corps actively engages in nation-building, disaster relief, community development and ecological protection across the region.

AIIMS Raipur Hosts Guest Lecture on Climate Change and Health, Launches 7th Edition of Community Medicine Textbook
articles.full_content:
Prof. Dr. Sanjay Zodpey highlights need for climate-responsive public health systems and preparedness 7th edition incorporates latest developments in community medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics and preventive medicine
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Raipur organised a guest lecture and book launch at the Swami Vivekanand Auditorium on Monday, bringing together senior faculty members, academic leaders, postgraduate residents, undergraduate students and other members of the institute for an academic discussion on emerging public health challenges.
The programme featured a guest lecture by Prof. Dr. Sanjay Zodpey, President, Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI), on “Deciphering the Connect Between Climate Change and Health”. The lecture examined the growing interrelationship between climate change and human health and underlined the importance of strengthening public health preparedness to address emerging climate-related health challenges.
The programme commenced with lamp lighting and Saraswati Vandana in the presence of the dignitaries. Lt Gen Ashok Jindal (Retd.), Executive Director, AIIMS Raipur, formally introduced Prof. Dr. Sanjay Zodpey as the chief guest and guest speaker.
Addressing the gathering, Prof. Dr. Zodpey discussed the multifaceted health implications of climate change and emphasised the need to strengthen health systems, surveillance, preparedness and public health interventions in response to the changing environmental and epidemiological landscape. He highlighted the importance of integrating climate considerations into public health planning and healthcare delivery. Following the lecture, Prof. Dr. Zodpey was felicitated by AIIMS Raipur in recognition of his contribution to the field of public health and participation in the academic programme.
A major highlight of the event was the formal launch of the seventh edition (2026) of the Textbook of Community Medicine & Public Health. The updated edition covers contemporary developments in community medicine, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics and preventive medicine.
Prior to the launch, Dr. Aditi Chandrakar, Associate Editor, presented “What’s New in the 7th Edition?”, outlining the major additions, updates and academic features incorporated in the new edition. Lt. Col. Laxmikant Choudhary (Retd.), Associate Editor, subsequently presented an overview of the e-content and its key features, highlighting the digital academic resources accompanying the textbook.
The seventh edition was formally unveiled by the chief guest and other dignitaries, followed by a cake-cutting ceremony. The book launch was followed by academic reviews from faculty members of AIIMS Raipur. Prof. Dr. Anil K. Goel, Academic Head, School of Public Health, shared his academic assessment of the book, while Prof. Dr. Binu Mathew, Principal, College of Nursing, AIIMS Raipur, highlighted the importance of comprehensive public health knowledge for healthcare professionals and students
